text: But the girls found the back door blocked by the cook, Sadie, Hans, and the man from Godbers, who was telling them that a young man had been killed just below the house. <break time="0.8s" /> The dead man was a carter named Scott, whose horse had shied at a traction engine, throwing him out onto the back of his head, and he had left a wife and young children. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura, horrified, pulled Jose aside and insisted that they must stop the party at once, but Jose, who thought her sister was being absurd, only stared at her in astonishment. <break time="0.8s" /> The little cottages stood in a lane below the hill, and as children the Sheridans had been forbidden to set foot there because of the coarse language and what they might catch. <break time="0.8s" /> Think how the band would sound to that poor woman, Laura said, but Jose replied that if Laura stopped a band every time someone had an accident, she would lead a very strenuous life. <break time="0.8s" /> Laura ran to her mother, who was trying on a new hat, but Missus Sheridans first question was whether the man had been killed in their garden. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she placed her new black hat, trimmed with gold daisies, on Lauras head, saying that it had been made for Laura and was much too young for herself. <break time="0.8s" /> People like that do not expect sacrifices from us, she said coldly, and Laura went to her room, where the first thing she saw was a charming girl in the mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps her mother was right, she thought, and she decided that she would think about the poor mans family again after the party was over.
